title: Name-Change Intake
description: Sample intake flow for helping a user identify basic name-change workflow needs while minimizing sensitive data.

allowed_jurisdiction_questions: What state are you filing in?
Do you know which court or county handles this filing?
Are you using a court form or instruction page already?
jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: Jurisdiction is needed before Pro-One can point to specific court instructions or forms.

intake_goal.primary_goal: Identify the user's basic name-change workflow and route them to source-backed next steps.
allowed_goals: Identify likely workflow category.
Ask minimum jurisdiction questions.
Explain common process steps.
Provide a checklist of information the user may need.
Flag document and filing boundaries.
prohibited_goals: Tell the user the petition is ready to file.
intake_goal.goal_notes: The intake should keep helping with practical, source-grounded process information without claiming legal sufficiency.

required_questions: What state or court system is this for?
Are you trying to change your own name or understand the process for someone else?
Do you already have court forms or instructions?
optional_questions: Do you need help finding the correct court page?
Do you need a checklist of possible documents?
Are you looking for fee waiver information?
conditional_questions: Is this for a minor, only if the user says the request involves a child?
Is there a safety or sealed-record concern, only if the user raises privacy or safety issues?
Is there an upcoming hearing or filing date, only if the user mentions timing?
prohibited_questions: Ask for a Social Security number.
Ask for full financial account numbers.
Ask for sensitive background details before they are needed.
questions.question_notes: Ask only what is needed to route the user to a safe workflow and source-backed process steps.

data_limits.data_limit_notes: The intake should use summaries and avoid collecting more facts than needed.

sensitive_data.sensitive_data_notes: Sensitive details should be summarized only when needed for routing or safety.

support_routing.routing_notes: Risk routing should not end support. It should keep the user moving through safer, narrower, source-backed help.

deadline_signals: The user reports an upcoming hearing.
The user reports a filing deadline.
The user reports a court notice with a response date.
high_risk_signals: The request involves a minor.
The user reports safety or domestic violence concerns.
The user reports sealed-record concerns.
The user is unsure which court applies.
unsafe_request_signals: The user asks Pro-One to invent facts.
The user asks Pro-One to hide required information from the court.
The user asks Pro-One to guarantee court approval.
risk_signals.risk_signal_notes: When risk signals appear, Pro-One should continue with issue spotting, court resources, checklists, and source-backed next steps.

outputs.output_notes: Outputs should help the user continue through the process without overstating what Pro-One can decide.

privacy.privacy_notes: The intake should remind users not to share unnecessary sensitive information.

review.review_notes: Sample intake definition only. Not approved for production use.

success_criteria: The intake asks only minimum needed questions.
The intake does not ask for prohibited sensitive data.
The intake keeps helping in a safe mode when risk appears.
The intake does not claim document readiness or legal sufficiency.
known_failure_modes: Abandoning the user when a risk signal appears.
Treating general information as court-specific guidance.
Implying a document is ready to file.
evaluation.evaluation_notes: Evaluation fixtures should test ordinary name-change intake and higher-risk variants involving minors, privacy, and deadlines.

title: Discovery Deadline Intake
description: Sample intake flow for urgent civil discovery questions where Pro-One should continue with safer deadline-aware support.

allowed_jurisdiction_questions: What state or court is the case in?
Is this state court, federal court, or another forum?
Do the discovery requests mention a response date?
jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: Jurisdiction matters because discovery rules and response timing can vary.

intake_goal.primary_goal: Identify discovery type, timing concern, and safe support mode without drafting final responses or choosing objections.
allowed_goals: Identify whether the issue involves interrogatories, requests for production, requests for admission, or another discovery request.
Ask for the user's understanding of the deadline.
Help the user organize what was received.
Provide a practical checklist.
Flag objections, privilege, admissions, and sanctions as risk areas.
prohibited_goals: Decide whether to admit or deny a request.
Tell the user to withhold responsive documents unlawfully.
intake_goal.goal_notes: Urgency should trigger safer support, not abandonment.

required_questions: What type of discovery request did you receive?
What court or jurisdiction is the case in?
What deadline do you believe applies?
Are you asking for help understanding the request, organizing a response, or identifying next steps?
optional_questions: Do any requests involve privileged, confidential, medical, financial, employment, or business information?
Have you received a motion to compel or sanctions threat?
Do you need a checklist for organizing responses?
conditional_questions: Ask for the exact request text only if needed and encourage redaction.
Ask whether a request is for admission only if the user says they received admissions.
Ask about a sanctions threat only if the user mentions a missed deadline or motion.
prohibited_questions: Ask for full financial account numbers.
Ask the user to paste confidential material unless necessary and redacted.
Ask the user to provide facts so Pro-One can invent objections.
questions.question_notes: Urgent discovery intake should reduce overwhelm and ask only the next useful question.

data_limits.data_limit_notes: Use summaries and redacted excerpts whenever possible.

sensitive_data.sensitive_data_notes: Discovery often involves sensitive information. Intake should not request full records unless absolutely needed for safe explanation.

support_routing.routing_notes: Even with an imminent deadline, Pro-One should keep helping by organizing the issue, flagging risks, and providing a checklist while avoiding final legal decisions.

deadline_signals: The user says a response is due today.
The user says a response is due tomorrow.
The user says the deadline already passed.
The user has received a motion to compel.
The user has received a sanctions threat.
high_risk_signals: The request involves admissions or denials.
The request may involve privileged information.
The request may involve confidential business records.
The user is considering withholding documents.
The user is unsure whether an objection applies.
unsafe_request_signals: The user asks Pro-One to invent responses.
The user asks Pro-One to hide responsive documents.
The user asks Pro-One to make a privilege determination.
The user asks Pro-One to decide whether to admit or deny without user-provided facts.
risk_signals.risk_signal_notes: Urgent discovery signals should trigger focused support: identify the request, identify the believed deadline, organize materials, flag risk, and suggest free or low-cost help options when appropriate.

prohibited_outputs: Admissions or denials chosen for the user.
Instructions to hide, destroy, or withhold evidence unlawfully.
outputs.output_notes: The output should help the user act quickly while avoiding final legal decisions.

privacy.privacy_notes: The intake should warn users to redact sensitive or privileged content when possible.

review.review_notes: Sample intake definition only. Not approved for production use.

success_criteria: The intake keeps helping during urgent discovery scenarios.
The intake does not invent responses or objections.
The intake flags deadline and sanctions risk.
The intake asks for redacted or summarized information.
The intake refuses unsafe requests while continuing safe support.
known_failure_modes: Telling the user to stop using Pro-One because the issue is urgent.
Collecting privileged or sensitive material unnecessarily.
evaluation.evaluation_notes: Evaluation fixtures should include same-day deadlines, missed deadlines, requests for admission, privilege concerns, and sanctions threats.

title: Subpoena Intake
description: Sample intake flow for subpoena questions where Pro-One should provide source-backed issue spotting and urgent support without deciding compliance or validity.

allowed_jurisdiction_questions: What court, agency, or authority issued the subpoena?
What state or jurisdiction is listed?
Does it ask for testimony, documents, or both?
jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: Subpoena obligations, response options, service issues, and timing depend on the issuing authority and jurisdiction.

intake_goal.primary_goal: Identify subpoena type, dates, issuing authority, and risk signals while continuing with safe support.
allowed_goals: Help the user understand what the subpoena appears to request.
Ask for key dates in a limited way.
Identify whether testimony or documents are involved.
Flag sensitive, privileged, or confidential materials.
Provide a checklist of urgent next steps.
prohibited_goals: Tell the user to ignore a subpoena.
Decide whether the user must comply.
Help destroy, hide, or withhold evidence unlawfully.
intake_goal.goal_notes: Subpoena intake should prioritize clear, practical, urgent support while avoiding legal determinations.

required_questions: Did you receive a subpoena or are you trying to understand one?
What court, agency, or authority issued it?
Does it ask you to appear, produce documents, or both?
What date is listed for appearance, production, or response?
optional_questions: Are you a party, witness, business, employer, records holder, or other recipient?
Does it request medical, financial, employment, confidential business, or privileged information?
Do you need help making a checklist of what the subpoena asks for?
conditional_questions: Ask whether the user is considering objecting only if they mention objection concerns.
Ask whether sensitive records are involved only if the request appears to involve records.
Ask whether there is a near deadline only if a date appears in the subpoena.
prohibited_questions: Ask the user to paste full sensitive attachments without redaction.
Ask for full medical or financial records.
questions.question_notes: Subpoena intake should be calm, focused, and practical.

data_limits.data_limit_notes: Collect only enough information to identify the subpoena type, urgency, and safe support mode.

sensitive_data.sensitive_data_notes: The intake should encourage summaries instead of full document disclosure.

support_routing.routing_notes: Subpoena support should continue in an urgent, source-backed, issue-spotting mode rather than ending assistance.

deadline_signals: The subpoena has a near appearance date.
The subpoena has a near document-production date.
The user received the subpoena shortly before the listed date.
high_risk_signals: The subpoena demands testimony.
The subpoena requests sensitive records.
The subpoena requests privileged or confidential information.
The user is considering ignoring it.
The user wants to object or move to quash.
unsafe_request_signals: The user asks Pro-One to tell them to ignore the subpoena.
The user asks Pro-One to decide validity of service.
The user asks Pro-One to draft final objections.
The user asks for help hiding, destroying, or withholding evidence unlawfully.
risk_signals.risk_signal_notes: Subpoena risk should route to issue spotting, deadline awareness, and free or low-cost help options while continuing practical support.

prohibited_outputs: A final decision on subpoena validity.
A final decision on compliance obligations.
Instructions to hide, destroy, or withhold evidence unlawfully.
outputs.output_notes: Outputs should help the user understand the subpoena, organize key dates, and identify safe next steps.

privacy.privacy_notes: The intake should caution against sharing full sensitive records or privileged material.

review.review_notes: Sample intake definition only. Not approved for production use.

success_criteria: The intake continues helping with urgent subpoena issues.
The intake does not decide validity or compliance.
The intake does not tell users to ignore subpoenas.
The intake uses summaries or redaction for sensitive material.
The intake flags testimony, sensitive records, and near deadlines.
known_failure_modes: Abandoning the user because the subpoena is urgent.
evaluation.evaluation_notes: Evaluation fixtures should include testimony subpoenas, business-record subpoenas, nonparty subpoenas, and near-deadline subpoenas.

title: Small-Business Demand Letter Intake
description: Sample intake flow for helping a small business organize facts for a demand letter or dispute communication.

allowed_jurisdiction_questions: What state is the business or dispute connected to?
Is this related to a contract, invoice, refund, service issue, or another dispute?
Has a court, agency, lawyer, or opposing party sent anything already?
jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: Jurisdiction may matter for legal prerequisites or deadlines, but general organization and communication help can continue.

intake_goal.primary_goal: Help a small business organize user-confirmed facts for a professional demand or dispute communication.
allowed_goals: Identify the dispute type.
Collect only user-confirmed facts.
Organize payment, contract, invoice, or service information.
Provide a checklist or user-confirmed draft when safe.
Flag lawsuits, deadlines, regulated activity, or legal threats for safer support.
prohibited_goals: Provide a legal opinion on liability.
intake_goal.goal_notes: Demand-letter intake may support practical drafting when the user confirms all facts and the matter is not high risk.

required_questions: Who is the letter or communication going to?
What result are you asking for?
What facts support the amount or remedy requested?
optional_questions: Is there an invoice, contract, receipt, or written communication?
What deadline would you like to request for a response?
Has the other side already threatened legal action?
conditional_questions: Ask whether the dispute is high value only if the amount appears significant.
Ask whether a lawsuit or subpoena exists only if the user mentions formal papers.
Ask whether regulated activity is involved only if the business type suggests it.
prohibited_questions: Ask for full financial account numbers.
Ask for trade secrets unless necessary.
Ask for facts the user does not know so Pro-One can make the letter stronger.
questions.question_notes: The intake should help the user organize facts without pressuring them to overstate the dispute.

data_limits.data_limit_notes: Use summaries and avoid including unnecessary financial or confidential business information.

sensitive_data.sensitive_data_notes: The intake should avoid collecting full account numbers, trade secrets, or privileged communications.

support_routing.routing_notes: The intake should keep helping small businesses organize facts and communicate professionally while narrowing when risks appear.

deadline_signals: The user mentions a statute of limitations.
The user has received a lawsuit or court deadline.
The user has received an agency notice.
The user needs to satisfy a pre-suit demand requirement.
high_risk_signals: The dispute involves a large amount of money.
The dispute involves regulated business activity.
The user wants to threaten criminal action.
The other side is represented.
The user has received formal legal papers.
unsafe_request_signals: The user asks Pro-One to include false statements.
The user asks Pro-One to threaten unlawful action.
The user asks Pro-One to harass or intimidate the recipient.
The user asks Pro-One to fabricate evidence or documents.
risk_signals.risk_signal_notes: The intake should refuse false or abusive content while continuing with factual, professional communication support.

prohibited_outputs: A guarantee of payment or settlement.
A demand letter based on invented facts.
outputs.output_notes: Outputs should help the user communicate clearly based on confirmed facts.

privacy.privacy_notes: The intake should remind users not to include unnecessary financial or confidential business information.

review.review_notes: Sample intake definition only. Not approved for production use.

success_criteria: The intake uses only user-confirmed facts.
The intake avoids unsupported threats.
The intake keeps helping after refusing unsafe language.
The intake minimizes sensitive business data.
The intake flags lawsuits, agency notices, and regulated activity.
known_failure_modes: Inventing facts to strengthen the letter.
evaluation.evaluation_notes: Evaluation fixtures should test unpaid invoices, contract disputes, refund requests, threats, and formal-paper scenarios.

title: Virginia DC-402 Defendant Information Intake
description: Proposed minimum-facts intake for identifying a served Virginia small-claims Warrant in Debt and routing questions safely.

allowed_jurisdiction_questions: What state and court are shown?
Does the form say DC-402 or Warrant in Debt — Small Claims Division?
What return date and time are printed?
jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: If document or division is unclear, do not give Virginia-specific procedural guidance.

intake_goal.primary_goal: Identify whether the user appears to have a served Virginia small-claims DC-402 and understand their information goal.
allowed_goals: Confirm form title and listed court.
Record the printed return date as user-provided.
Offer source links and organize questions.
prohibited_goals: Choose a response, defense, settlement, or removal strategy.
Determine service validity or a deadline.

required_questions: What form title or number is printed?
What return date and time does the warrant show, if any?
What would you like help understanding?
optional_questions: What general claim category is shown?
conditional_questions: Is the listed date today, passed, or soon?
prohibited_questions: Do not request Social Security or full account numbers.
Do not request unredacted papers or privileged communications.

deadline_signals: Return date is imminent, today, passed, or unclear.
high_risk_signals: Court or form cannot be confirmed.
unsafe_request_signals: User asks which response or defense to choose.

success_criteria: Collects minimum facts and routes uncertain dates safely.
known_failure_modes: Asking for unnecessary sensitive data or inventing procedural requirements.

notes: Proposed intake; collect only what is needed and remind users the service has no persistent user storage.
